newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's unemployment falls to 9.3 pct in March.
newsitem.headline: Canada's unemployment falls to 9.3 pct in March.

text.p: Statistics Canada said on Friday the unemployment rate fell to 9.3 percent in March from 9.7 percent in February. The March unemployment rate is the lowest since November 1995.
Note - Labor force, employment and unemployment in millions, on seasonally adjusted basis.
A Reuters survey of economists had forecast the unemployment rate to drop to 9.6 percent.
Overall employment rose by 60,900 to 13.8 million in March, the biggest gain since August 1996. Full time employment rose by 30,200 from the month before, and part time employment grew by 30,700.
The rise in employment levels were a reversal of last month's loss of 18,700 jobs and brought gains in employment to 133,000 since last September, Statistics Canada said.

The federal agency said the gains in employment were concentrated among adults, with employment in March rising 33,000 for men and 25,000 for women. About four out of five of these jobs were full time.
But there was little change in total employment for young Canadians in March, the agency said. Full time employment for youth fell 16,000 and offset part-time growth of 19,000.
Statscan said employment increases in March were mainly in the service sector, with advances in business and personal services as well as in trade.

In the goods sector, a gain in manufacturing employment offset losses in other industries, the agency said. Manufacturing employment rose by 37,000, the first employment increase since August 1996. But employment in construction fell in March by 14,000, leaving gains at 44,000 since May 1996.
